question: Scope the two redirects left by the causal-FA2 kill: (1) widening the sealed gqa_pair candidate past candidate_scope=final_fixed32_b4_full_graph_only to the non-captured mixed-pass tree calls at b=2..3; (2) deciding the dfwd draft-head causal FA2 sliver from banked evidence.

headline.one_line: Both redirects were scoped against the wrong denominators. The 7.07 s mixed-pass block is ~79% unrecoverable (occupancy, not geometry), while a 16.47 s block the brief never named -- the IN-STEP b=3 FULL-graph tree calls -- is reachable with the same widening, on the existing acceptance instrument, and is worth ~4x more.
headline.mechanism_correction: The gqa_pair gain is a WAVE-COUNT gain, not merely a half-empty-tile gain. Occupancy is exactly 1 CTA/SM (98304 B dynamic smem vs GB10's per-SM limit; 48 SMs -- banked in results/fr13_attack_ladder_analysis_20260808). Stock grid (1,b,24) = 24b CTAs -> ceil(24b/48) waves = 1,1,2,2 for b=1,2,3,4. gqa_pair grid (3,b,4) = 12b CTAs -> 1 wave for every b in 1..4. The candidate can therefore only pay where stock needs 2 waves: b=3 and b=4. At b<=2 stock already fits one wave, the paired CTA runs the identical serial K loop, and the expected wall gain is ZERO (GPU-time still halves; wall does not).
headline.wave_model_evidence: Out-of-step per-launch: b=3 3.9011 ms / b=1 1.9449 ms = 2.006 -- two waves against one, to 0.3%. In-step: b=3/b=1 = 2.158, b=4/b=2 = 1.946. Same-wave pairs differ only by context length (b=2/b=1 = 1.280 in-step, 1.261 out-of-step). The kernel is NOT bandwidth-bound (banked: 69.75 ms at width 4 against a ~17.75 ms bandwidth floor), which is why halving KV traffic alone buys nothing when the wave count does not fall.

q_a_is_the_kernel_correct_as_built_for_b.answer: The KERNEL BODY is already b-agnostic. B=4 enters at exactly four places, all of them launch-side or assertion-side, none of them in an address computation or a loop bound.

audit_of_every_B_dependency.role: grid.y in the launcher: dim3 grid(query_heads_per_kv/kHeadsPerCTA, sequences, kv_heads)
audit_of_every_B_dependency.fix: launch grid.y = params.b (runtime); the value is never read inside the kernel except by static_asserts

audit_of_every_B_dependency.site: flash_fwd_kernel.h:692-693 and :1603-1604, same assertion in compute_attn_1rowblock_splitkv and compute_attn_splitkv

positive_proof_that_nothing_else_binds_B: kStaticSequences is referenced ONLY at flash_fwd_kernel.h:681-682, 691 (kStaticQueryBatch = sequences != 0), 692-693, 726, 1591-1592, 1601-1604. It never enters a pointer, an extent, or a loop bound.

static_query_offset (flash_fwd_kernel.h:95-111) returns bidb * kStaticQueryRows(32) * row_stride -- a compile-time contraction of cu_seqlens_q that is exact for ANY b as long as every request contributes exactly 32 query rows (total_q == 32*b, cu_seqlens_q == [0,32,...,32b]). Independent of b.
block_table = params.block_table + bidb * params.block_table_batch_stride (:872-873) -- per-request, runtime.
gQ / gOaccum head-pair layouts (:898-937, :1463-1497) use params.q_row_stride / q_head_stride / o_row_stride / o_head_stride -- runtime.
gLSEaccum (:1498-1523) uses bidh * params.total_q + bidb*32 with stride (1, params.total_q) -- params.total_q is RUNTIME, so the unpadded-LSE layout is already correct at total_q = 64 and 96.

row_offset_oaccum / row_offset_lseaccum (:1456-1460) are the only expressions carrying params.b, and both are Split-only; Split is false for this trait (static_assert(!Split) inside the kHeadsPerCTA==2 branches).

StaticPagedKVStrides page = 2*1024*4*256, row = 4*256, head = 256 encode page_block_size, kv_heads and head_dim -- the literal 4 is kv_heads, NOT batch. Nothing in the static tile or the static strides is a function of B.
q_a_is_the_kernel_correct_as_built_for_b.same_so_or_new_tu: SAME KERNEL BINARY IS SUFFICIENT IN PRINCIPLE -- but not with the sealed .so, because grid.y is baked at compile time (StaticLayout::sequences) and, for FULL-graph traffic, again at cudagraph capture time. The B1 gate needed its own TU only because a template specialization cannot carry two different `sequences` values in one binary; making grid.y runtime removes that constraint entirely and would let ONE TU serve b=1..4. So: no new TU, no new kernel, ~10 lines of C++ -- but it is still a source change, therefore a new .so, therefore a mandatory re-seal.

zero_so_change_alternative_PADDED_B4.idea: Leave the sealed .so bit-for-bit alone. At b=3, present the call to FA2 as a canonical b=4 call with one inert shadow request: cu_seqlens_q = [0,32,64,96,128], total_q = 128, seqused_k[3] = 64 (one K block -> the 12 shadow CTAs are near-free), block_table row 3 = a pinned valid page, tree_bias already the (4,32,32) tagged shape the selector materialises today. The 33-clause TORCH_CHECK passes unmodified; the kernel launches its compile-time grid (3,4,4) = 48 CTAs = exactly one wave, i.e. the same wall as a native b=3 gqa_pair launch. Discard rows 96:128 of O and columns 96:128 of LSE.
zero_so_change_alternative_PADDED_B4.why_the_shadow_is_free: Per-request independence (see q_b). A shadow request with seqused_k = 64 runs one masking step and exits; its 12 CTAs cost ~1/16 of a real CTA and fit inside the same single wave.
zero_so_change_alternative_PADDED_B4.why_naive_padding_would_NOT_work_and_thi: Padding b=2 -> b=4 gives 48 CTAs, exactly stock's 48 at b=2 -- zero gain. The gain exists only because at b=3 stock needs 72 CTAs (2 waves) and padded-gqa_pair needs 48 (1 wave). This is another statement of the wave model, and it is why the padded trick is worth nothing at b<=2.
zero_so_change_alternative_PADDED_B4.cost: q and out are already slices of persistent buffers (out=output[:num_decode_tokens] in the patched tree_attn decode branch), so a zero-copy widen to [:128] may be available; otherwise a private (128,24,256) bf16 staging buffer costs ~1.18 MB in + 1.18 MB out per layer, ~0.2-0.4 ms/step against a ~25.6 ms/step gain (<1.6% overhead).
zero_so_change_alternative_PADDED_B4.what_it_buys: The .so sha256 af9e9f24..., size 299813360, FA2 HEAD 2921022186..., and the six per-file source digests in scripts/fr13_fa2_qrow32_gqa_pair_gate.py ALL SURVIVE UNCHANGED. The parent scope.json named the mandatory decode-candidate re-seal 'the single largest hidden cost item'; this route deletes it. What still moves: patch_source_sha256, pass_sidecar_sha256, the candidate_scope token, and a NEW live paged A/B byte gate proving output[0:96] and lse[:,0:96] are byte-identical between native-b3-stock and padded-b4-candidate.
risks_that_must_be_gated_not_assumed: Stale Q rows 96:128 may contain NaN/Inf. Harmless by construction (no cross-CTA reduction) but the gate must show O[0:96] is bit-identical with the shadow rows deliberately poisoned with NaN.
output[96:128] is written with garbage. Must prove no downstream consumer reads past num_actual_tokens in the b=3 graph.
block_table[3][0] must be a valid page index; write it explicitly rather than trusting stale contents.
All padding ops must be cudagraph-capturable and captured INTO the b=3 graph.

q_b_accumulation_order_at_b_2_3.answer: SAFE, and provable at source level -- stronger than the b=4 argument, because it is a restriction rather than an extension.
q_b_accumulation_order_at_b_2_3.argument: The candidate has Split=false and no combine launch, so there is no cross-CTA reduction of any kind. Each CTA owns exactly one (bidb, kv_head, head_pair) and writes O rows and LSE entries no other CTA touches. For a FIXED request r, the ordered sequence of K blocks the CTA visits is n_block_max-1 down to 0 with n_block_max = ceil_div(seqused_k[r], 64); the page addresses come from block_table[r]; the bias comes from tree_bias[r]; the softmax running max/rescale chain is per-row and private. NONE of these is a function of b. Therefore the bytes written for request r at b=3 are identical to the bytes written for request r at b=4 with the same (seqused_k[r], block_table[r], tree_bias[r], Q rows). b<4 removes CTAs; it never reorders an accumulation.
q_b_accumulation_order_at_b_2_3.the_only_true_dependency_on_b: params.total_q, used solely as the LSE row stride (flash_fwd_kernel.h:1512) -- an address, not an operand. It is already runtime.
q_b_accumulation_order_at_b_2_3.tier: Tier-A compatible. The exact-math byte rule is satisfied by construction; the live byte gate is confirmation, not discovery.

q_c_dispatch_and_sentinel_for_non_captur.in_step_b3: NO new sentinel and NO new dispatch channel. The mixed-pass sentinel problem does not exist here. The call already routes torch.ops._vllm_fa2_C.varlen_fwd_tree_bias with a tagged (b,32,32) fp32 bias whose stride(0) IS the sentinel 0x20014 (131092) -- and note the sentinel is a REAL stride that the kernel dereferences (tree_bias + bidb*131092, flash_fwd_kernel.h:144-145), so a b=3 tagged tensor is simply torch.empty_strided((3,32,32),(131092,32,1)) (or (4,32,32) on the padded route, which is what the selector builds today). What changes is python: capture_num_reqs != 4 bypass, _fr13_fa2_qrow32_b4_production_capture_end's batch_size != 4 guard, _fr13_fa2_qrow32_live_ab_replay's batch_size != 4 guard, and five b-dependent clauses in _fr13_fa2_qrow32_b4_geometry_mismatches: query.shape == (128,24,256), cu_seqlens_q.shape == (5,), seqused_k.shape == (4,), block_table.shape[0] == 4, tree_bias.shape in ((32,32),(4,32,32)).
q_c_dispatch_and_sentinel_for_non_captur.mixed_pass: Confirmed as the parent scope.json described: mixed passes reach the selector eagerly and take the `outside_capture` bypass (there is no capture context and no graph_id). Engaging there needs a mixed-pass admission predicate, a (forward_pass_index, layer_name) capture key, and a fixed-chunk-boundary evidence pin. All of that is real work for a 0.42%-of-window prize that the board cannot measure.

redirect_2.question: Is the dfwd draft-head causal FA2 call's max_seqlen_q <= 32 (tile half-empty, premise holds) or 33..64 (full tile, dead)?

evidence_chain.primary_measurement: In the width-4 nsys sqlite, all 540 in-step causal splitkv launches (one per fr13.fixed32.dfwd range, 540/540) are preceded on the same stream by vllm::reshape_and_cache_flash_kernel with gridX == 32 * gridY, with zero exceptions: (b=1, 32 tokens) x4, (b=2, 64) x74, (b=3, 96) x237, (b=4, 128) x225. reshape_and_cache_flash's gridX is literally slot_mapping.size(0), the unpadded token count (csrc/cache_kernels.cu: num_tokens = slot_mapping.size(0); dim3 grid(num_tokens)).
evidence_chain.why_it_is_a_proof_not_an_average: The b=1 bucket has ONE request and 32 tokens. That pins 32 query rows for a single request and closes the 33..64 branch outright; the b=2/3/4 buckets then only have to be uniform, which the exact 32*b totals over 540 launches establish.
evidence_chain.corroboration_downstream: The post-attention triton_red_fused_..._rms_norm and silu_and_mul_per_block_quant_kernel at fixed offsets +4 and +7 both carry gridX = 32*b (225/225 and 237/237), so FA2 consumed and produced all 32*b rows -- num_decode_tokens = 0, the 'prefill' slice is the whole tensor.
evidence_chain.independent_calibration: The non-causal cfwd tree-verify call, whose max_seqlen_q == 32 is HARD-ASSERTED in source (scripts/fr13_patch_fa2_tree_bias.py:4475, 5116, 5994 -- ('max_seqlen_q', int(max_seqlen_q) == 32)), produces a byte-identical 32*b trace signature.
evidence_chain.call_site: The dfwd FA2 call is the FR13_FA2_PREFILL_NATIVE branch (scripts/fr13_patch_fa2_tree_bias.py ~6918-6928: flash_attn_varlen_func(q=query[num_decode_tokens:num_actual_tokens], ..., max_seqlen_q=prefill_meta.max_query_len, causal=True)). The draft head's 32-row query has query_len>1 so TREE_ATTN's metadata builder classifies it as prefill. The decode tree-verify call is causal=False because FR13_SLOT_REORDER=1 (container_env.txt:461) drives _fr13_sr_causal_flag() (patcher 6798-6811) to False.
evidence_chain.topology_corroboration: --speculative-config num_speculative_tokens=31 with a 31-path speculative_token_tree; 31 drafts + 1 root = 32 physical rows. Banked as physical_rows_root_inclusive=32 (scripts/fr13_run_b4_draft_head_m32_timing.sh:94 and :495) and physical_rows_per_request=32 / total_physical_rows=128 (scripts/fr10_phase4_patch_vllm_tree_gdn.py:1612-1613).

the_cheap_route_that_the_parent_did_not_.claim: The dfwd causal call does NOT need a causal paired kernel. At seqlen_q = 32 with kBlockM = 64, Is_causal=1 is EXACTLY reproducible by the already-sealed non-causal kernel plus a lower-triangular 32x32 tree_bias.
the_cheap_route_that_the_parent_did_not_.derivation: FA2 causal admits query row i (0..31) to key n <= i + seqlen_k - seqlen_q = i + K - 32. Keys 0..K-33 are admitted for every row; over the final 32 keys, column j is admitted iff j <= i -- exactly lower-triangular. apply_tree_bias under kStaticQueryTile hard-codes tree_bias_rows = cols = 32, q_offset = k_offset = 0, row_stride = 32, col_stride = 1, and anchors at context_len = actual_seqlen_k - 32, i.e. precisely the final 32 key columns (flash_fwd_kernel.h:146-156). A {0, -INFINITY} lower-triangular mask therefore writes -INFINITY into exactly the entries mask.h would.
the_cheap_route_that_the_parent_did_not_.n_block_max_is_unchanged: flash_fwd_kernel.h:754 takes n_block_max = min(ceil_div(seqlen_k, 64), causal_bound), so the causal clamp only ever reduces it; at m_block = 0 and seqlen_q = 32 the causal bound ceil_div(64 + K - 32, 64) never binds. Both instantiations visit the identical ordered K-block sequence.
the_cheap_route_that_the_parent_did_not_.check_inf_is_unchanged: causal path Check_inf = Is_causal || Is_local || !Is_even_MN = true; non-causal path Check_inf = !Is_even_MN = true. Same template argument.
the_cheap_route_that_the_parent_did_not_.what_it_buys: The 3 compile-time barriers the parent identified (static_assert(!Is_causal && !Is_local) at flash_fwd_kernel.h:1304, 1359, 1392) are simply never reached, because the call is dispatched as Is_causal=0. The 12-20 agent-hours of causal-kernel authoring, the rebuild, and the full re-seal ALL DISAPPEAR. What remains is python: route the draft head's prefill-branch call through varlen_fwd_tree_bias with a pinned lower-triangular tagged mask, plus a new target-layer pin (the MTP head is 1 FA2 call per dfwd, not 16) and a byte gate.
residual_risks_that_must_be_gated: n_masking_steps differs (causal: ceil_div(64,64)+1 = 2; non-causal: 1). The masking-step loop and the main loop run the identical gemm -> bias/mask -> softmax_rescale_o -> gemm_rs sequence, so byte-equality is expected but is NOT proven by inspection -- it must be a byte gate, not an assumption.

The 33-clause TORCH_CHECK must be satisfied by the draft head's own call: h == 24 (confirmed, gridZ = 24), h_k == 4, d == 256, page_block_size == 1024, and the k/v cache strides 2*1024*4*256 / 4*256 / 256. The MTP head has its OWN KV cache layer; if its cache geometry differs the check fails CLOSED and nothing engages. Verify offline before building.
b == 4 && total_q == 128 restricts the route to the 225 width-4 dfwd launches unless sub-target 1A's widening (or the padded-b4 trick) lands first.

what_this_does_not_claim: No live measurement of any kind was taken. CPU-only, offline, over already-banked captures and source.

The 0.3682 recovery fraction is a TRANSFER from the measured b=4 result (29.50 ms/step over 16 layers against 5.0123 ms/launch), not a measurement at b=3. The wave model that justifies the transfer is supported by the per-launch ratios but is a model.

The b<=2 zero-gain prediction follows from the wave model plus the banked fact that the kernel sits ~3.9x above its bandwidth floor. If the kernel is more bandwidth-sensitive than that figure implies, b=2 would pay something and sub-target 1B's verdict would soften -- it would still be unmeasurable on the available basis.

The mask-equivalence derivation for redirect 2 is an argument about which acc_s entries receive -INFINITY and in what order the K blocks are visited. It predicts byte-equality; it does not establish it. A byte gate is mandatory.
